name: Hemoflow
subtitle: Blood flow, pressure, shear
shortDescription: Narrow a vessel and watch the flow collapse. Seven hands-on labs for blood-flow physics, fully offline.
longDescription:
Pull a vessel narrower and watch the flow collapse. Hemoflow is a hands-on lab for the physics of blood circulation, built for physiology and medical students and for anyone who wants to feel why radius matters so much.

Seven labs, one idea: change a number, see the whole system respond.
- Wall layers: cut open an aorta, artery, arteriole, capillary, vein with valve or vena cava, drawn to scale from published wall dimensions.
- Poiseuille bench: set radius, length, pressure drop and haematocrit. Resistance, flow, mean velocity, wall shear stress and Reynolds number update live while cells stream through a 3D vessel.
- Stenosis and aneurysm: narrow a vessel or let it bulge. See the pressure drop, the throat jet, the shear, the wall tension, and how tissue demand changes what a lesion costs.
- Pulse wave: drive an aortic arch with heart rate, stroke volume, peripheral resistance and arterial stiffness. The pressure wave, mean pressure and pulse pressure come from a Windkessel model.
- Murray branching: grow an arterial tree with the minimum-work rule and bend the exponent to see wall shear drift.
- The whole circuit: pressure, total area, velocity and organ shares of cardiac output, from rest to hard exercise.
- Predict: five new questions every day, built from the same engine as the labs, with a streak and a mastery map.

Save any setup to your notebook and add your own notes. Everything works offline.

Accuracy matters in training, so every formula and number is listed in the in-app Accuracy and sources page with two references and known simplifications. Anything schematic is labelled on screen, and a Report an error link goes straight to us.

Education only. Hemoflow is not medical advice and is not for judging any patient or scan.
